STEP 1 - Vessel type: The vessel has a curved inner wall rising well above the food, with a visible shadow inside and the food sitting well below the rim. This is a deep bowl (a stainless steel mixing bowl).

STEP 2 - Vessel size:
a) Type cue: a stainless steel mixing bowl like this is typically a medium-to-large serving bowl, roughly 20-25 cm.
b) Reference cue: cherry tomatoes are about 3 cm across. Several tomatoes plus pepper pieces span roughly 7-8 tomato lengths across the visible inner bowl, which gives about 22-24 cm.
Reconciled width: about 23 cm.

STEP 3 - Food items:
- Capacity = 0.35 x 23^3 / 1000 = 0.35 x 12167 / 1000 = 4.26 L (4260 ml).
- Fill: the food is a small loose heap sitting well below the rim, roughly 2-3 cm of depth against a bowl depth of about 10 cm. Fill ≈ 0.25 (fraction of depth).
- Food volume = 4260 x 0.25 x 0.25 ≈ 266 ml.
- Items by count and share:
  - Cherry tomatoes: about 7 whole or halved, roughly 60% of the visible food. Estimated weight: 7 x 15 g = 105 g (cross-check: 266 ml x 0.6 x 0.6 g/ml ≈ 96 g). Use about 100 g.
  - Red bell pepper pieces: about 25% share, 266 x 0.25 x 0.6 ≈ 40 g.
  - Green and yellow bell pepper pieces: about 15% share, 266 x 0.15 x 0.6 ≈ 24 g.

STEP 4 - Hidden food: No base layer is visible; the bowl floor is largely bare steel, so no hidden items are added.

STEP 5 - kcal per 100 g (raw vegetables): cherry tomato ≈ 18 kcal/100 g; bell pepper (red, green, yellow) ≈ 28-31 kcal/100 g, use 30.

Totals: about 164 g of food. Energy ≈ 100 x 0.18 + 64 x 0.30 ≈ 18 + 19 ≈ 37 kcal.
